chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakki (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi said, that Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i said, on the authority of his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfili, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sinan, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, has given the believer a guarantee. I asked, 'What is it?' He replied, 'He guarantees him - if he acknowledges His Lordship, and Muhammad's (peace be upon him and his family) prophethood, and 'Ali's (peace be upon him) Imamate, and carries out what is obligatory upon him - that He will settle him in His Presence (jiwar). I said: 'By Allah! This is a blessing with which none of the blessings bestowed upon the children of Adam can compare!' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do little, and you will enjoy much.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific guarantee Allah gives to believers who acknowledge the Imams and fulfill their duties?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the ultimate divine promise of *jiwar* (dwelling in God's presence) as contingent upon the triad of *Tawhid*, *Nubuwwah*, and *Imamah*, alongside the fulfillment of obligatory duties. This concept elevates the believer's status beyond mere salvation to intimate proximity with the Divine, a core tenet in Shia eschatology. The Imam’s concluding advice, 'work a little to enjoy much,' underscores the disproportionate spiritual reward for consistent, sincere practice of the fundamentals.
